statement: In Spanish public works, the contractor may receive payments on account for preparatory operations such as site installations and materials stored on site, secured by a guarantee (Article 240.2 of Law 9/2017; Article 155 of Royal Decree 1098/2001).
details: Monthly works certificates (certificaciones) are the usual basis for payment; check Article 240.1 in the consolidated text.

statement: An energy efficiency certificate (Royal Decree 390/2021) is required for new buildings and for existing buildings or units sold or let to a new tenant; agents must show it when marketing.

Under the Building Act (Ley 38/1999 de Ordenación de la Edificación, Article 17), building agents answer for material damage for 10 years (structural defects), 3 years (habitability defects) and 1 year (finishing defects), counted from acceptance of the works without reservations.
details: Once damage appears within the period, the claim must be brought within two years (Supreme Court ruling 1211/2023). Record the acceptance date as the start of every period.

statement: Building works in Spain need a municipal works licence (licencia de obras) or, for works the regional law allows, a declaración responsable; occupation needs a first-occupation licence or its regional equivalent.
details:
Procedures are regional and municipal. This card only names the instruments; the Building Act gives the national framework.

Source note: the Building Act gives the national framework only; the licence instruments named here are general knowledge to verify with the municipality.

statement: In Spanish public contracts, periodic price revision (Article 103 of Law 9/2017) applies only where the tender documents provide it, covers only raw materials, intermediate goods and energy, and never overheads or profit; Law 11/2023 widened it to all contract types.
details: Check the formula and official index named in the pliego before accepting a revised claim.

statement: Law 32/2006 limits subcontracting chains in construction to three levels, with justified exceptions approved by the site management and recorded in the Libro de Subcontratación, which every construction site must keep.
details: Breaches are serious or very serious infringements and create joint liability for labour and social security obligations.

statement: Contractors and subcontractors in Spanish construction must be registered in the Registro de Empresas Acreditadas (REA) of their region (Law 32/2006, Royal Decree 1109/2007); registration is valid nationwide.
details: Check REA registration before awarding any subcontract package.

statement: Resale of property in Spain pays transfer tax (ITP) at rates set by each autonomous community, while new dwellings pay IVA plus stamp duty (AJD) at regional rates.
details: Never quote an ITP or AJD rate without the region's current table.

statement: In Spain, the first delivery of a new dwelling by the developer pays 10% IVA (Article 91.Uno.1.7 of Law 37/1992), protected housing (VPO, special regime) 4%, and commercial premises, offices and most construction for companies the general 21%.
details: Up to two parking spaces and annexes sold with the dwelling share the 10% rate. Secondary source; confirm with AEAT binding rulings. The Canary Islands use IGIC instead.

statement: Renovation works on a private dwelling can carry 10% IVA instead of 21% only when conditions are met (private residential use, the dwelling more than two years old, materials below the legal share); otherwise 21% applies to the whole job.
details: Check the conditions on every renovation quote; secondary source.
